note: Reviewed CDB90 match 36, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Reviewed full battle of 4 October 1674, Turenne against Bournonville, independently identified in the Entzheim municipal bulletin (December 2021, printed pp. 30–31). The explicit Enzheim → Entzheim redirect binds the original CDB title to Q1143181 through the separately reviewed alias. Both initial-strength rows cover this engagement: FR ARMY 22000 and IMP ALLIED ARMY 31700, with personnel casualties 3500 and 2500, not deaths. These remain CDB estimates: the municipal account gives roughly 6500 combined losses, so it is identity/date evidence and does not certify the CDB sum of 6000. Later Brandenburg reinforcements are not added. Each mixed field army remains a single local military unit; no component totals, equipment or tactical movements are inferred. Article alias review (2026-09-22; Q1143181; Battle_of_Enzheim -> Battle_of_Entzheim): Reviewed the explicit redirect at revision 457515601 and the target article revision 1370440030 with its Q1143181 link; Wikidata Q1143181 lists Battle of Entzheim as its English sitelink. This confirms article identity only, not CDB quantities. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name FR ARMY): Municipal account identifies the French force commanded by Turenne. The original FR ARMY aggregate is retained, without allocating its infantry and cavalry. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name IMP ALLIED ARMY): Municipal account identifies Bournonville’s Imperial force. The original IMP ALLIED ARMY remains one local aggregate; the old Holy Roman Empire identity Q12548 is replaced by this field army, retaining both original citations. No later Brandenburg arrivals are included.
